messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
Below is a concise summary of the most important Texas traffic‑law provisions you’ll encounter as a driver, rider, or passenger. For detailed legal advice consult a licensed attorney or official state sources such as the Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS) or the Texas Legislature’s website. | Topic | Key Statutes / Provisions | Practical Takeaway | |-------|---------------------------|--------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • § 545.001 – General speed limit
• § 545.002 – Speed limits on highways
• § 545.003 – Posted speed limits on rural roads | • Maximum posted speeds vary from 55–75 mph depending on road type.
• If no sign appears, default to 35 mph in residential areas, 45 mph elsewhere. | | **Seat Belt & Child Restraint Laws** | § 545.021 – Seat belts required for all occupants
§ 545.022 – Children under 8 years old must ride rearward-facing until age 2, forward-facing thereafter with booster seats until 5th grade or 48 inches tall | • Failure to wear a seatbelt can result in a $50 fine plus demerit points.
• Children not properly restrained may face higher penalties ($200+). | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | §§ 542.011–542.019 – Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) limits, impaired driving definitions, penalties | • Legal BAC limit is 0.08% for drivers over 21.
• Penalties include fines up to $1,000, license suspension, mandatory education programs, and possible jail time. | | **Texting While Driving** | § 545.031 – Texting prohibition for drivers aged ≥18 | • Using a handheld device while operating a vehicle is illegal unless using hands-free technology.
• Violation carries a $100 fine and potential points. | | **Cell Phone Use** | § 545.032 – Hands‑free devices allowed only when the phone is mounted securely | • Mounts must keep the screen within eye level and allow full control of the vehicle. | | **Pedestrian Right-of-Way** | § 545.041 – Pedestrians have right-of-way at crosswalks and intersections | • Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing marked or unmarked crosswalks. Failure results in a $150 fine. | | **School Bus Stop Rules** | § 545.042 – Vehicles must stop for school buses stopping to pick up/drop off children | • Stopping includes both directions; failure incurs a $250 fine. | | **Lane Discipline** | § 545.043 – Lane discipline rules for passing, lane changes, and overtaking | • Improper lane usage can lead to a $25 fine per violation. | | **Traffic Signal Violations** | § 545.044 – Red light running, yellow-light violations, and other signal infractions | • Red-light running typically triggers a $300 fine + points. | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | § 545.045 – Vehicle registration requirements, inspection stations, and emissions testing | • Unregistered vehicles risk towing and impoundment. | | **Parking Regulations** | § 545.046 – Parking restrictions, handicapped spaces, loading zones | • Illegal parking can incur a $30 ticket and towing costs. | ### Enforcement Agencies * **Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV):** Handles registrations, licensing, and administrative penalties. * **County Sheriffs/Police Departments:** Enforce local ordinances and handle tickets. * **State Police:** Investigate serious offenses including DUIs and highway safety issues. ### Resources for More Detail 1. **TexCode Online** – Official copy of the Texas Transportation Code. *URL:* https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/?link=TXTC&chapter=545 2. **Texas DPS Traffic Law Handbook** – PDF guide covering common violations. *Download link:* https://www.dps.state.tx.us/sites/default/files/documents/Texas_Driver_License_Handbook.pdf 3. **Legislative Reference Library of Texas** – Legislative history and bill summaries. *Website:* https://lrl.texas.gov/ --- #### Quick Tips: * Always check your local county ordinance because some cities impose stricter speed limits or additional signage. * Keep your driver's handbook handy—many courts accept it as proof of knowledge during hearings. * If you receive a citation, consider contacting a qualified traffic‑law attorney before contesting it online; many attorneys offer free initial consultations. Feel free to ask if you'd like deeper dives into any specific section, how to appeal a ticket, or guidance on navigating court procedures!
